title: Regional Readiness Orchestrator + Fallback Variant Selector
creator: Daniel Brooks
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a Regional Readiness Orchestrator (RRO) that drives smart region selection, tier-aware routing, and fallback model-variant selection during multi-region failover. The goal is to provide predictable cutovers with minimal latency/backpressure, preserve cached state where possible, and ensure customer workloads remain within SLOs during incidents and planned maintenance.

Goals:
- Produce an orchestration service that computes a readiness score per region+tier+model-variant in real time. Scores should incorporate health probes, capacity headroom, KV/prefix cache priming status, model warmup percentiles, and recent error/latency trends.
- Route by policy: primary->tiered fallbacks->regional priority list->model variant fallback, with pluggable policies per customer/route.
- Provide gating and quorum checks before warm-standby activation to avoid noisy cutovers.
- Support graceful pre-warming of KV/prefix caches and model weights in target regions using shadow traffic and staged priming.
- Integrate with Console for operator controls (force activate, override routing, pre-emptive priming) and with tracing/observability for post-mortems.

Design notes / architecture:
- Readiness scoring: combine signal inputs into a 0-100 score. Inputs include: health probe pass rate (last 1m), p90 latency delta vs baseline, GPU utilization headroom, available concurrency slots, KV-cache hit ratio and priming completeness, model-variant warmup percentile (token throughput), recent error-rate slope, and active maintenance flags. Weights are tunable per-customer.
- Orchestrator responsibilities: maintain regional inventories, compute scores, emit routing directives to the Smart Router, run preflight priming jobs (i.e., shadow requests to populate KV/prefix cache and lazy weight load), and execute cutover playbooks with stepwise traffic shifts.
- Tier routing: traffic should prefer same-tier capacity (e.g., enterprise-dedicated -> enterprise-dedicated fallback) before falling back to lower tiers. Each tier has a mapping to compatible model-variants to preserve behavior.
- Fallback model variants: model graph must be annotated with fallback relationships (e.g., standard->quantized-int8->smaller-llamax). The selector should consider compatibility of tokens, function-calling contracts, and output distribution drift risk.
- Priming strategy: stage I: control-plane scheduled prefix KV seeding for top N customers; stage II: shadow traffic at 1-5% to validate latency and output; stage III: ramp readiness gating once cache hit ratio and warmup throughput thresholds are met.
- Quorum gating: require N healthy nodes in the target region per model-variant + cache primed at >=80% + failover score delta above threshold for at least T seconds. Quorum parameters are tunable per region and per release.
- Rollback: automated rollback if error rate spikes > 2x baseline in the first 3 minutes after cutover or if p95 latency exceeds SLO by > 20% for more than 30s.

Observability and metrics:
- New metrics: region_readiness_score{region,tier,model_variant}, priming_progress{region,customer}, kv_cache_hit_ratio{region,customer}, model_warmup_tokens/sec, region_activation_events, fallback_selector_decisions.
- Dashboards: per-route readiness timeline, priming task history, recent fallbacks and reason tree, cost delta during priming.
- Alerts: readiness degradation per region, priming failures >3 attempts, activation rollback triggered.

Operational playbooks (high-level):
1) Preflight: run readiness checks for planned maintenance; operator can schedule priming window.
2) Automated warm failover: orchestrator evaluates scores, performs staged priming, executes stepwise traffic shifting and validates metrics at each step.
3) Emergency cutover: if primary region fails, orchestrator will select highest-scoring compatible region+tier and activate with conservative traffic caps then follow fast validation.
4) Postmortem: orchestrator exports decision rationale and metric traces to Console and links to incident ticket.

Security and compliance considerations:
- Priming uses customer prefixes and may touch cached customer data; must obey data residency rules and only prime within permitted regions.
- All priming requests must be labeled and logged; KMS usage for model artifacts remains enforced.

Acceptance criteria:
- RRO running in canary region and producing readiness_score metric for 3 model families.
- Smart Router respects directives for traffic shifts in canary test and fails safe to previous routing on rollback conditions.
- KV/prefix priming task can complete for a 10k prefix sample within configured window and reflect in priming_progress metric.
- Console exposes per-route operator controls and a visualization of readiness score and priming status.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MR/Regional+Readiness+Orchestrator
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/running/pull/2741
- Simulation dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/priming/simulations

Risks / trade-offs:
- Aggressive priming increases cost and may temporarily inflate CPU/GPU usage. We mitigate with rate-limited shadow traffic and cost dashboards.
- Model-variant fallback introduces potential semantic drift. We'll tie fallback decisions to eval suites per-route and record fallbacks to notify product owners.
- Overly conservative quorum gating can increase time-to-failover; parameters must be tuned with chaos tests.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Daniel Brooks: Initial spec posted. Raised trade-offs around priming cost vs availability. Linked simulation results in Confluence.

2026-03-04 - Lena Chen: Implemented basic readiness_score calculator prototype. Found that KV priming completion has high variance across customers. Filed follow-up ENG-128451 to instrument per-customer priming latency.

2026-03-07 - Marco Alvarez (SRE review): Suggested adding a short-circuit path for emergency cutover when regional control-plane is unreachable; recommended default rollback thresholds be slightly stricter for public cloud regions.
2026-03-09 - Design review (Lena): Console control prototypes uploaded. Need an operator mode to 'pre-approve' priming windows to avoid accidental cross-region data residency violations.
2026-03-12 - Daniel Brooks: Canaries scheduled for 2026-03-18 in eu-west-1 using runtime-1.22. PR for Smart Router integration opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/338
